title: The Broken Umbrella
learning_objectives: Listen to a longer story and explain a character's plan
Identify cause and effect across pages
parent_prompts: Before: Tim's umbrella breaks on the way to school. What could he use instead?
After page 4: Why did the plastic bag not work well?
After: Which idea was best? Why do you think so?

pages.text: Rain drummed on the roof. Tim grabbed his umbrella and ran for the bus. Halfway down the lane, the wind caught it. Snap! One of the metal arms broke.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim (red cap) in a lane in heavy rain, umbrella inside-out with one bent spoke.
pages.audio_script: Rain drummed on the roof. Tim grabbed his umbrella and ran for the bus. Halfway down the lane, the wind caught it. Snap! One of the metal arms broke.

vocabulary.definition: A cloth roof on a stick that you hold over your head in the rain.
vocabulary.example: Take an umbrella, it might rain.

pages.image_alt: Tim in a lane in heavy rain, umbrella inside-out with one bent spoke.

pages.text: Now the umbrella flopped to one side. Rain ran down Tim's neck. "I need a new plan," he said.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim under a sagging umbrella, one shoulder soaked.
pages.audio_script: Now the umbrella flopped to one side. Rain ran down Tim's neck. I need a new plan, he said.
pages.image_alt: Tim under a sagging umbrella, one shoulder soaked.

pages.text: Plan one: a big leaf from the banana tree. It was wide and green. But it was heavy, and it dripped straight onto his head.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim holding a huge banana leaf over himself, water pouring off its tip onto his cap.
pages.audio_script: Plan one: a big leaf from the banana tree. It was wide and green. But it was heavy, and it dripped straight onto his head.
pages.image_alt: Tim holding a huge banana leaf over himself, water pouring off its tip.

pages.text: Plan two: a plastic bag from his pocket. It kept his hair dry. But it crackled, and it blew away at the first gust.
pages.illustration_brief: A white plastic bag flying off Tim's head into the wind.
pages.audio_script: Plan two: a plastic bag from his pocket. It kept his hair dry. But it crackled, and it blew away at the first gust.

vocabulary.definition: A sudden strong push of wind.
vocabulary.example: A gust blew my hat off.

pages.image_alt: A white plastic bag flying off Tim's head into the wind.

pages.text: Plan three: Tim looked at the broken umbrella again. Two arms were fine. He folded the broken side down and held the good side up, over his head, like a shield.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim holding the half-folded umbrella tilted over his head against slanting rain.
pages.audio_script: Plan three: Tim looked at the broken umbrella again. Two arms were fine. He folded the broken side down and held the good side up, over his head, like a shield.

vocabulary.definition: Something you hold up to keep things from hitting you.
vocabulary.example: She used the book as a shield from the sun.

pages.image_alt: Tim holding the half-folded umbrella tilted over his head against slanting rain.

pages.text: It was not perfect. His left arm got wet. But his head stayed dry all the way to the bus stop.
pages.illustration_brief: Tim at a bus stop shelter, half-umbrella in hand, one wet sleeve, grinning.
pages.audio_script: It was not perfect. His left arm got wet. But his head stayed dry all the way to the bus stop.
pages.image_alt: Tim under a bus shelter, half-umbrella in hand, one wet sleeve, grinning.

pages.text: On the bus, a girl looked at his strange umbrella. "It broke," said Tim. "So I made it half an umbrella." She laughed. "Half is better than none."
pages.illustration_brief: Inside a bus, Tim showing the half-umbrella to a girl with plaits, both smiling.
pages.audio_script: On the bus, a girl looked at his strange umbrella. It broke, said Tim. So I made it half an umbrella. She laughed. Half is better than none.
pages.image_alt: Inside a bus, Tim showing the half-umbrella to a girl with plaits.

pages.text: That night, Dad fixed the broken arm with tape. But Tim kept the half-umbrella trick in his head, just in case.
pages.illustration_brief: Dad at a table taping the umbrella spoke; Tim watching.
pages.audio_script: That night, Dad fixed the broken arm with tape. But Tim kept the half-umbrella trick in his head, just in case.
pages.image_alt: Dad at a table taping the umbrella spoke; Tim watching.

quiz.prompt: Why did the plastic bag not work?
quiz.explanation: Page 4 says it blew away at the first gust.

quiz.prompt: What was wrong with the banana leaf?

options.text: It was heavy and dripped on his head

quiz.explanation: Page 3 says it was heavy and dripped straight onto his head.

quiz.prompt: Why did Tim keep the half-umbrella trick in his head?

options.text: In case an umbrella breaks again

quiz.explanation: Page 8 says he kept the trick in his head just in case, meaning in case it happens again.

quiz.prompt: What is this story mostly about?

options.text: Trying plan after plan until one works

quiz.explanation: Tim says he needs a plan (page 2) and tries three plans until the third works (page 5).

quiz.prompt: Tell a grown-up Tim's three plans and which one worked.
quiz.rubric: not yet: says umbrella broke only; with support: two plans with prompting; independent: leaf dripped, bag blew away, half-umbrella worked
quiz.explanation: Naming all three plans in order with their results shows the problem-solving structure was followed.
